subject: seahorse
reasoning:
I'm planning a seahorse model with the SDK, thinking through a compact upright design around 0.15-0.16m tall, possibly with a small coral or seagrass base to anchor the curled tail to the floor.

I'm mapping out the skeletal structure with coordinate points for the spine: a hips root joint, a neck chain arching up to the head with a forward-tilted snout, and a tail chain curling down and back from the hips.

For the tail, I'm setting catmull points that spiral inward, tapering the radius from 0.016 to 0.003 so the tip sinks toward the floor without clipping through it. For the body itself, I'm considering whether to loft the whole trunk as one continuous sweep from tail tip through hips to head, or treat the tail and neck as separate sweeps joined at a thicker belly section.

Instead I'm defining a single body sweep with the hips as the root joint, splitting it into front and back chains by finding the closest parameter on the curve to the hips, then driving the radius as a function of arc-length distance from that root so the belly bulges wider sideways and front-to-back near the hips.

Taper is tighter toward the neck and tail tip, using a circular cross-section for simplicity. The head and jaw are being handled as separate joints parented off the end of the front chain, with a snout formed by upper and lower rods connected via a jaw joint.

Still working out the coronet spikes, eyes, and dorsal fin membrane placement...

Still shaping the fin outline... I want vertical ribs running across it, so I'll set the stripe axis to "z" rather than "y" to get the right band orientation. Then I'm adding small pectoral fin extrusions positioned behind the head on each side.

Now I'm working out body stripes and countershading—placing darker rings along the body using a modulo pattern on position, with a base orange tone and a darker ring color, plus a lighter belly tone for contrast.

For the dorsal spikes, I'm reconsidering the approach since the clock-based angle from the sweep doesn't work well on a vertical path. I'm shifting to casting rays outward from points inside the body toward the back direction to find proper surface attachment points for the spine bumps.

Now I'm settling on colors: amber body tones (#e9a23b base, darker #b9651f shading, pale #f3d28a belly), warm fin color, and dark eyes with a white highlight dot. I'm also starting to sketch out a coral base structure as a stem.

Still refining tail coil geometry...

Now I'm checking overall height: head crest sits around 0.19 with body top near 0.17, which looks consistent. I'm laying out the body curve points from tail tip through hips to neck to form a belly bulge using catmull interpolation.

Mapping the neck and head joint positions, I want the chest to bow forward slightly before curving back toward the head. I'm also reconsidering the tail curl radius since it may self-intersect with the body radius, so I'm recalculating the tail's radius profile along its length to taper it down appropriately.

Now I'm defining a radius function along the body's length, blending chest, belly, and neck sizes with sinusoidal tapering for smooth transitions between segments.

Writing section/color code...

Working out the head's local orientation and joint position off the last front joint, then placing the cranium sphere and starting the snout shape relative to the head bone.

Still defining jaw joint and rod...

Now I'm placing the eyes symmetrically on each side of the head, with a dark pupil sphere offset outward and a small white highlight for shine.

Then I'm working on the crown spikes, arranging a row of small spike shapes along the top of the head, each with a base and tip position tilted back and up to form a ridge.

Next I'm adding small cheek spines and setting up a pectoral fin near the chest-neck area using a fan-shaped outline extruded along the body's depth axis.

Now I'm tilting the fin outward slightly, adjusting its attachment bone, and checking the extrusion shape stays convex so it won't self-intersect. Then I'm placing a dorsal fin along the back near the hips.

Checking the fin placement coordinates against the body surface, I'm estimating where the back curve sits at each y-value so the fin base stays roughly flush against it, even though the exact boundary math gets a bit approximate here.

Nudging the fin base to z -0.026 to avoid a visible gap. Now I'm thinking through the stripe pattern on the fin -- bands stacked along the z-axis to form a fan-like ray effect -- and planning spines along the back by sampling points along the body path and placing small cones wherever they hit the surface.

Setting up the body sweep's bone structure and color scheme, deciding on 8 sides with rounded caps, then checking that the hip joint position lines up correctly with the corresponding body path point.

Finishing the base lathe outline with a closed polygon shape, keeping the bone reference on core, then moving to eye and mouth colors with a tiny nostril detail skipped. I'm now focused on writing the final TypeScript code, including typed interpolation functions and underscore-prefixed callback params, plus checking the body's path length property.
